correctness.rationale: The degree-two anticanonical map is the double cover of the plane branched over the smooth quartic. Its rational sections are indexed by 31 rational lines; a section is smooth genus one precisely when the homogeneous quartic restriction has four simple geometric roots. The 3 coordinate lines always qualify; the 4 lines at each pair of nonzero equation coordinates qualify exactly when the corresponding branch coefficients do not sum to zero. For 16 full-support lines, coordinate rescaling reduces to x+y+z=0. One can independently check the asserted discriminant test as follows: a tangent there has ax³=by³=cz³≠0. Write A=1/a, B=1/b, C=1/c, and scale to x³=A, y³=B, z³=C. Then x+y+z=0 implies (A+B+C)³=27ABC. Conversely if the last equality holds, take cube roots x,y and set z=(A+B+C)/(3xy); now z³=C. Factor x³+y³+z³−3xyz into the three cube-root-of-unity linear forms and rotate the cube roots as needed to make x+y+z=0. Thus the homogeneous tangent test is D=(ab+ac+bc)³−27a²b²c², which expands into the frozen polynomial modulo 5. This test includes geometric contacts, with no degree-drop problem. The normalized coefficient table yields the stated frequencies. For (1,1,2), coordinate-line counts are 2,2,4, mixed-support counts are 8,10,10 in groups of four, and the remaining 16 counts are all 6. Every base value is nonzero, so nonsquare scaling complements each line count to 12 and the total count to 62. The distinct totals 36 and 26 distinguish the twists; permutations and common square scaling exhaust the isomorphism presentations in scope. An independent exact homogeneous-resultant scan reproduced the complete enumeration and spectra.
residual_risks: Replay tests every triple and line in scope, not arbitrary quartics, extension fields, or arbitrary degree-two del Pezzo surfaces. No reliance on recorded expected outputs.

evidence: Any smooth curve with a rational point has a rational tangent, so tangent-free diagonal quartics must be pointless. Three distinct nonzero coefficients in F5 necessarily include an opposite pair, giving a rational point. For repeated coefficients scale to (1,1,b); b=3 makes the triple sum zero and b=4 makes a pair sum zero. Only (1,1,1) and (1,1,2) remain, up to common scaling and permutation; the two census rows then distinguish 16 and 0 tangents.
A point count of a rational anticanonical member requires the quadratic-character values along its six rational base points; the branch-bitangent census only detects tangency of certain restrictions.

evidence: Geometric smoothness of a rational anticanonical section is exactly rational-line transversality to the branch quartic, and a rational point of the dual means a rational tangent line, not necessarily a rational contact point.
Asgarli–Freidin's transverse-free condition is the opposite extreme: no transverse rational line.
equivalent_formulations.reasoning: On a smooth pointless quartic a rational tangent must have a nonrational contact. Its other Frobenius-conjugate contact has equal multiplicity and Bézout forces two double contacts. Thus for those quartics the rational tangent and rational bitangent line sets coincide, making the census materially relevant to branch transversality.

value.rationale: The side-by-side spectrum of the two twists describes how the 31 smooth rational genus-one members are distributed, not just whether a smooth section exists or how many rational points lie on the surface. The support-type formula explains how the full spread of 15 to 31 arises in the natural exact diagonal F5 family, including branch curves with rational points omitted from the pointless census. The exact spectra offer concrete tests for arithmetic Bertini and twist comparisons. No additional value is predicated on rediscovering the covered branch example or its all-transverse property.
